project.name: ussefy Portfolio
project.goal: A small, honest, hand-crafted-feeling portfolio with a fixed sidebar and a content area, introducing one person across three roles: front-end developer, graphic designer, social media manager.
project.originalBrief: Create a lite React portfolio with a sidebar (avatar, nav: Home/About/Services/Contact, copyright, social icons) and a main area. Home shows only a name and an animated, one-by-one cycling list of specialities (Front-End Developer, Graphic Designer, Social Media Manager) centered in the main box. The design must feel human-made, not AI-generated: no gradients, no border-radius, no shadows.

enhancedPrompt: Build a lightweight React portfolio site with a two-column layout: a fixed-width sidebar and a fluid main content area. The sidebar contains, top to bottom: a square (not circular) avatar photo with a hard 1px edge, the person's name in small caps beneath it, a vertical navigation list with four items (Home, About, Services, Contact) using plain text and a solid square/underline indicator for the active or hovered state (no pills, no rounded highlight backgrounds), then — pushed to the bottom of the sidebar — a row of monochrome outline social icons (no filled glossy icons) followed by a small monospace copyright line. The main area renders one of four views depending on the selected nav item. On Home, show only the person's name as a large serif headline and, directly beneath it, a single line of text that cycles through three specialities — 'Front-End Developer', 'Graphic Designer', 'Social Media Manager' — one at a time, using a typewriter-style type/hold/delete animation with a blinking solid block cursor, both vertically and horizontally centered in the main box. About, Services and Contact are simple, content-first pages with no decorative flourishes. Visually, the entire site must read as deliberately hand-designed rather than AI-generated: flat solid background colors only (absolutely no gradients), zero border-radius anywhere (every corner is a hard 90° corner), and no box-shadows or drop-shadows of any kind — depth and separation come only from flat color blocking and thin 1px solid hairline borders/dividers. Typography should carry the personality of the page instead of decoration: pair a characterful serif display face for the name/headings with a plain humanist sans for body copy and a monospace face for labels, nav numbering, and the copyright line. Motion should be restrained and purposeful — the only animation on the whole site is the specialities typewriter loop on Home; everything else is static, with simple, quick (150–200ms) opacity/color transitions on hover and focus. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by freezing the typewriter into a static crossfade or plain list. The layout must collapse gracefully on mobile: the sidebar becomes a slim top bar rather than a bottom sheet or hamburger drawer, since there are only four nav items.

designPhilosophy.coreDirective: Looks like it was laid out by a person with a ruler and a limited set of solid inks — not generated by a template.
hardRules: No gradients anywhere — every fill is a single flat solid color.
No border-radius anywhere — every element (avatar, buttons, cards, inputs) has hard square corners.
No box-shadow or drop-shadow anywhere — separation comes from flat color blocks and 1px solid hairline borders only.
Avoid the common 'AI portfolio' tells: no warm-cream + terracotta serif combo, no near-black + neon-accent combo, no glossy circular avatar, no glassmorphism, no big rounded pill buttons.
designPhilosophy.howDepthIsCreated: Depth and hierarchy come from color contrast (paper vs ink vs sidebar tone), spacing rhythm, and thin solid dividers — never from elevation effects.
designPhilosophy.signatureElement: The typewriter-style specialities line on Home is the one deliberately animated, memorable moment. Everything else on the site stays quiet and static so that moment lands.

paper.role: Main background — a natural, slightly grey-warm paper tone (not glossy cream).

sidebarSurface.role: Sidebar background — one shade darker than paper, flat, no gradient.

ink.role: Primary text, headings, icon strokes, borders.

inkSoft.role: Secondary text — descriptions, captions, inactive nav items.

accentOlive.role: Primary accent — active nav indicator, links, cursor block, focus ring.

accentOchre.role: Secondary accent — hover states, small highlights, used sparingly.

display.style: normal, generous letter-spacing on headings only

mono.usage: Nav item numbering, copyright line, specialities cursor line, form labels

borders.radius: 0px everywhere — hard corners only, including avatar image and buttons.
borders.style: 1px solid var(--ink) at low opacity (e.g. 15–25%) for hairline dividers between sidebar sections and between main content blocks.

designTokens.shadows: none — explicitly disabled. Use flat color blocking or a 1px border instead of any elevation.

motion.easing: linear or ease-out only — no bouncy/spring easing, keep it mechanical and honest
motion.reducedMotion: All non-essential transitions disabled; typewriter loop replaced with a static crossfade list when prefers-reduced-motion is set.

sidebar.verticalRhythm: Avatar and name at top, nav list in the middle, social icons + copyright pinned to the bottom via flex column with justify-content: space-between

main.behavior: Fluid width, scrollable independently of sidebar
main.homePageCentering: display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; on the main box so the name + animated specialities sit dead-center of the visible area, both axes.

responsive.belowBreakpoint: Sidebar collapses into a slim horizontal top bar: avatar shrinks and moves inline next to the name, the 4 nav items lay out in a single horizontal row (they fit without needing a hamburger menu), social icons + copyright move below the nav row or into a thin footer strip.
responsive.reasoning: Only 4 nav items — a hamburger drawer or bottom sheet would add unnecessary UI chrome for such a small menu, and would work against the 'simple, human, lite' brief.

components.name: Sidebar
components.notes: Single flat-color panel, no card/box treatment around it — it IS the background.

components.name: Avatar
components.shape: Square or rectangular image, hard edges, 1px solid ink border (optional), NOT a circle — a circular cropped avatar reads as a generic template default.
components.size: ~96px square on desktop, ~48px inline on mobile top bar

components.name: NavMenu
components.activeState: Solid square marker (▪) or a solid underline drawn with border-bottom — never a rounded pill or background highlight.
components.accessibility: Rendered as a <nav><ul> list of <button> or <Link> elements; active item gets aria-current="page".

components.name: SocialLinks
components.style: Monochrome outline/stroke icons only (e.g. lucide-react), single color = ink, no filled glossy icon packs, no circular icon backgrounds.
components.notes: Swap the exact platform list for whichever accounts are actually used — Behance/Instagram matter more here given the graphic-design and social-media-manager angles.

components.name: Copyright
components.typography: mono font, caption size, inkSoft color

components.name: MainArea
components.behavior: Renders one of Home / About / Services / Contact based on the active nav selection (local state — no router required for a 4-page lite site, though react-router-dom is a valid upgrade if real URLs are wanted).

components.name: AnimatedSpecialities
components.purpose: The signature animated element — see animationSpec below.

home.content: ONLY two elements, centered together in the middle of the main box: (1) the person's name as a large display-serif headline, (2) directly beneath it, the animated specialities line.
home.explicitlyExcluded: No hero image, no CTA buttons, no scroll hints, no background decoration — keep it as sparse as the brief asks.

exampleCopy.name: Youssef — replace with full name or brand name

about.content: Short first-person bio paragraph (3–5 sentences), plain body typeface, left-aligned, generous line-height. Optionally a small 'currently based in / working in' mono caption line beneath it (fits the multilingual FR/AR/EN, Morocco-based context if relevant).
about.explicitlyExcluded: No timeline graphics, no skill progress bars (these read as templated).

services.content: Three flat list rows or three-column blocks — one per speciality — separated by 1px hairline dividers, not cards with shadows.

items.title: Front-End Development
items.copy: Builds clean, functional interfaces and small web apps — from landing pages to full product UIs.

items.title: Graphic Design
items.copy: Designs visual identity, layouts, and print/digital assets that stay legible and on-brand.

items.title: Social Media Management
items.copy: Plans and runs content and posting schedules that keep an account active and consistent.

contact.content: A short line inviting contact + email address as plain text (mailto link) + optionally a minimal plain-HTML contact form: name, email, message — flat input fields with 1px solid borders, no rounded corners, no shadow focus glow (use a solid outline offset for focus instead).

animationSpec.technique: Typewriter cycle: type each word out character-by-character, hold, delete character-by-character, pause, move to next word, loop forever.

cursor.shape: solid block (▍ or a CSS ::after rectangle), not a thin line and not a rounded caret

animationSpec.easing: steps() / linear only — this is a mechanical typing effect, not an eased fade.

accessibility.ariaLive: polite region so screen readers announce each new speciality once, not every keystroke (use aria-live on the settled word, not the animating characters).
accessibility.prefersReducedMotion: Disable typing/deleting entirely; instead show all three specialities as a simple static stacked list or a slow 400ms opacity crossfade between them.

interactionStates.navHover: Text color shifts from ink to accentOlive over 150ms; underline draws in via border-bottom, no background fill.
interactionStates.navActive: Solid square marker appears to the left of the item, or a persistent underline; aria-current="page" set.
interactionStates.buttonHover: Flat color invert (ink background / paper text) instead of a shadow lift — keeps interactions honest and physical rather than floaty.
interactionStates.focusVisible: 2px solid ink (or accentOlive) outline with 2px offset on every interactive element — no glow, no blur.

accessibility.landmarks: Semantic <nav>, <main>, <footer> used correctly; skip-to-content link at the very top of the DOM.
accessibility.contrast: ink (#211D17) on paper (#F2EFE9) exceeds WCAG AAA; verify accentOchre against paper for any text use (borderline — reserve ochre for larger UI elements, not small body text).
accessibility.images: Avatar has descriptive alt text (e.g. 'Portrait of {Name}').
accessibility.motion: prefers-reduced-motion fully respected as described in animationSpec.

techStack.styling: Plain CSS with CSS custom properties (:root variables for every design token) or CSS Modules — deliberately avoiding Tailwind's default radius/shadow utility defaults and avoiding component libraries like MUI/Ant/Chakra, which bake in rounded corners and elevation by default.
techStack.routing: Local React state (activePage) for switching Home/About/Services/Contact is enough for a 'lite' single-page feel; react-router-dom is an optional upgrade only if real shareable URLs per section are wanted.
techStack.icons: lucide-react (or any stroke-based outline icon set) styled in a single flat color — avoids filled/glossy default icon packs.
techStack.fonts: Fraunces (display), IBM Plex Sans (body), IBM Plex Mono (labels/caption) — loaded via Google Fonts or self-hosted.

folderStructure: index.css                 (design tokens as CSS variables + global reset)
content.js               (name, bio, services array, contact info — all copy centralized here)

avoidedDefaults: Warm cream (#F4F1EA-ish) + terracotta serif combo — common AI-portfolio tell, so this spec shifts to a cooler grey-paper tone with an olive/ochre accent instead.
Near-black background + single neon accent — not used; kept a light paper-based palette since the brief called for something human and approachable.
Circular avatar with soft shadow — replaced with a square, hard-edged avatar to match the no-radius/no-shadow rule and to feel more like a printed ID card than a social-media profile pic.
Rounded pill nav buttons with background fill on hover — replaced with plain text + underline/marker, closer to a printed index or ledger.
designReviewNotes.whyTypewriterForSpecialities: A typewriter/terminal-style reveal fits the 'front-end developer' identity naturally (cursor, monospace-adjacent motion) while still reading as a warm, handmade touch rather than a generic fade-in carousel — and it's the one place motion is allowed to be a little playful, since everything else on the site is deliberately still.
